agent.preplan_summary: Three-storey Class A fire-resistive medical office building (1991) with six inferred medical life-hazard suites on floor 3; worst case is Suite 310 (dental, sedation, oxygen and nitrous oxide). Attack up Stair B (17 m, 26 m of hose via the standpipe), evacuate down Stair A to side A where Engine 1 is staged; hydrant H1 is 13 m from the building.

aar.summary: Fire in Suite 310 (dental office). Six people are accounted for: B1's two were carried out by the rescue team from a UWB fix, B2 was reached by a room search from a Bluetooth ring only, X1 was found by Engine 1 in the corridor with no app, B4 was reached in the more probable of two candidate positions, and B3 reported herself outside. Nine suites on floor 3 were never searched; from the building record, between 24 and 102 people could be in them during open hours. That is a range from floor area, not a count, and it is why the floor is not cleared.
went_well: B1 went from first ring to a fix in 19 s once the third puck landed
The ring for B2 was searched as a room, not walked to as a point
improve: B4 waited 148 s for a crew: both crews were committed
No puck reached the east side of the floor
follow_up: Search suites 300 to 308 before the floor is declared clear
File the Suite 309 occupancy question against the building record
Add the 310/311 door to the twin

limits: A ring is a range from one puck, not a position; two candidates are two places, not one.
Devices are not people: the cold device count is a band, and phones without the app cannot be identified.
Expected occupancy comes from floor area and a load factor: an estimate, never a head count.
An unscanned or silent suite is not cleared.
Crew positions are simulated; the interior twin is synthetic and may differ from the real floor.
